newsitem.title: SWITZERLAND: Swiss agree to Holocaust memorial fund.
newsitem.headline: Swiss agree to Holocaust memorial fund.

text.p: The Swiss government and banks agreed on Thursday to set up a Holocaust memorial fund as a gesture of goodwill towards world Jewish groups critical of Switzerland's wartime financial role, an official said.

Special Ambassador Thomas Borer told reporters after talks with senior executives of Swiss banks, insurance companies, the central bank and other businesses that details remained to be worked out and that no sum had yet been discussed.

"We certainly hope that this (fund) will be understood as a sign of our goodwill," Borer said, referring to demands from the World Jewish Congress and other critics that Switzerland make a gesture of remorse for profiting from World War Two.

Borer said his task force, charged with coordinating Switzerland's response to the crisis, would lead efforts to put together details of the fund, including how it should be organised and its exact purpose.

"Its goals will have something to do with the Holocaust in the widest sense," Borer said, naming projects to fight discrimination and racism as well as support for Holocaust survivors as possible aims.
Borer declined to say when the full concept could be ready and the fund created. But he said it was more a matter of weeks than of months.
